newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber retreats to end mixed, some new lows.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber retreats to end mixed, some new lows.

text.p: Early carryover short covering subsided and CME lumber futures retreated to post new contract lows in November and March before ending mixed, traders said.

Although the market appeared oversold and the single-family home sales report showed a 6.1 percent rise in June, prices eased on continued slow cash trade. A more careful study of the home sales report showed a very large downward revision in May sales which abated any June rise, traders said.

Demand for wood continues to be slower than the current pace of production, and that pace traditionally increases into the fall. The possibility that union coastal lumber workers in Canada and lumber companies were getting closer to a deal on a new contract also weighed on the market, they added.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $342 per tbf, down $4 from Friday and $10 under the last midweek level. They said trade was dull.
Lumber closed $0.50 per tbf lower to $3.00 higher with September up $0.20 at $336.70 and November off most at $334.30 per tbf.
